verdict.line: You lose if you let Apprehend connect and get stacked to enrage before level 6; you win if you trade during its cooldown and burst Haymaker off a tanked Decimate.

brief.thesis: Sett's Haymaker (W) is a bank-and-release ability — it only pays off after Sett has absorbed damage as Grit, which means Darius's own autos and Decimate hits are feeding Sett's burst. The matchup hinges on Darius's Apprehend (E, cooldown 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s): while it's down he has no way to punish Sett walking up, and once it's up it's the only tool that can drag Sett into Hemorrhage range. The 51.7% win rate over 5059 games matches the EVEN lane rating because whoever controls that cooldown window controls the trade.

theirWindow.what: Darius can hook from 535 range before you're in his face; he'll use it to force Hemorrhage stacks onto you uninterrupted, and if he reaches 5 stacks he enrages for massive bonus AD, so back off rather than greedily extending the trade.

yourWindow.what: Walk him down using Knuckle Down's (Q) move speed toward champions, trade autos freely since he can't hook you back in, and look to tank an auto or Decimate swing so Haymaker (W) has Grit stored before you release it.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks on repeated autos and ability hits during the long trades this lane forces, converting to AD and then healing at max stacks — directly countering Decimate's own sustain from hitting you with the blade.

summoners.why: Run in 95.6% of games at 52.2% win rate — Ignite punishes all-in trades before Darius hits level 6 and denies the healing he gets from landing Decimate's blade, locking in kills during the even-trade window.

playing.title: Trade when Apprehend is down
playing.detail: Darius's E (Apprehend, cooldown 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s) has no pull threat while on cooldown. Walk up and trade autos and Knuckle Down (Q) freely since he can't hook you back in if you try to disengage.

playing.title: Sandwich him for the E stun
playing.detail: Facebreaker (E) only stuns if enemies end up on opposite sides when pulled together — a single target on one side is just slowed. Position so a minion sits on his far side before you pull to lock the stun instead.

playing.title: Punish the Decimate wind-up
playing.detail: Darius's Q (Decimate) has a visible wind-up before the circular swing. The moment he commits to the animation, close distance and land your E pull — this is exactly the window OP.GG's own read on this matchup calls out.

playing.title: Bank Grit before releasing W
playing.detail: Haymaker (W) only pays off once you've absorbed hits. Let a Decimate swing or a couple of his autos land on you first so the true damage center hit and physical damage sides are worth casting.

playing.title: Respect 5 stacks of Hemorrhage
playing.detail: At max stacks Darius enrages for massive bonus AD. Disengage before he reaches that threshold rather than continuing to trade into an enraged Darius.

playing.title: Save R for his all-in
playing.detail: The Show Stopper (R, cooldown 120/100/80/80/80s) removes Darius from the fight for its duration and slows everyone near the landing spot. Hold it to answer his Noxian Guillotine engage rather than opening with it yourself.

playing.title: Close distance with Q, not blind walks
playing.detail: Knuckle Down (Q) grants move speed while moving toward enemy champions. Use it to close the gap Darius wants for his hook before he's able to use Apprehend on you.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample-size figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch. The tell, power curve, and in-lane tactical reasoning are my own analysis built from the ability mechanics, not scraped data.

stats.opponentTip: Manage your ddistance well to avoid being pulled by Darius’s (E). Use [E] when Darius uses (Q) to gain the upper hand in combat.
